claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-0:.../PlaceOrderLong.cs: 10-16 early returns; 18-22 `totalVnd += line.Quantity * line.UnitPriceVnd;`; 24-27 `if (customerIsLoyal) { totalVnd -= totalVnd * 10 / 100; }`; 29 `totalVnd += totalVnd >= 2_000_000 ? 0 : 30_000;` (fee only when < 2,000,000); 31-32 two Console.WriteLine (saving, email); 34 `return $"order placed, total {totalVnd}";`.

Line 26 `totalVnd -= totalVnd * 10 / 100;` mutates totalVnd in place; line 29, the next statement, compares that same totalVnd with 2_000_000. Execution (claim 3) confirms: 10% -> fee added (2010000), 5% -> no fee (2090000).

Ran it: scratch net10.0 console copying PlaceOrderLong.cs verbatim from stage-0 plus a copy with `* 5 / 100`, input new OrderLine(2, 1_100_000), customerIsLoyal=true. Output: "order placed, total 2010000" and "order placed, total 2090000" (saving lines print the same totals).

Lines 4-5: `// One method that checks, prices, saves and notifies. Four reasons to change` / `// one place, and no name for any of the four.` The lesson quotes the second sentence verbatim. Note: the comment sits above `public static class PlaceOrderLong` (line 6), not directly above the method (line 8) — see issue on section 5.

Definitional/opinion with a stated condition; no pinned-version document governs it. Lesson wording (§3 "together shape how expensive later changes are", §9 "a large part of what later changes cost") is hedged and consistent with the ledger. No docs opened for this claim.

After line 26, totalVnd is read on line 29 (fee), 31 (`saving order for customer {customerId}, total {totalVnd}`) and 34 (return). Line 32 is `Console.WriteLine($"sending an email to customer {customerId}");` — customerId only.

Inspected whole file at stage-0: the only comment (lines 3-5) says nothing about which total the fee uses; no variable or method names the original vs discounted total — there is only `totalVnd`, overwritten on line 26 before line 29 reads it. Statement ordering alone decides it.

Opinion with condition; follows from claims 2 and 6. "by accident" keeps it true: a fee rule given the discounted total as a named input would still change on a discount edit, but visibly, not by accident. No external source applies.

issues.quote: a one-character pricing edit reached the shipping fee
issues.text: Carried over from round 1, still unfixed here (§2 was fixed to "tiny edit"). Changing `10` to `5` replaces two characters with one; it is not a one-character edit. Unlisted factual claim.
issues.fix: Replace with "a one-number pricing edit reached the shipping fee" (and the vi equivalent).

issues.text: Unlisted evaluative claim, and it clashes with §8, which says the prerequisite lesson read `PlaceOrderLong` "for its length" (as too long). A junior sees the two lessons disagree.
issues.fix: Replace with "`Place` reads top to bottom with no tricks, yet" — or drop "short and".

issues.quote: The file's own comment, just above the method, names the problem
issues.text: The comment is on lines 4-5, above `public static class PlaceOrderLong` (line 6); the method `Place` starts on line 8. It is above the class, not the method.
issues.fix: Replace "just above the method" with "just above the class" (or "at the top of the file").

issues.quote: `PlaceOrderLong.Place` does four jobs in one method body: it checks the input, calculates the price, saves the order and notifies the customer.
issues.text: The four jobs are check, price, save, notify. But the lesson's surprise is discount -> shipping fee, and I cannot tell which job the fee belongs to. If it is part of 'calculate the price', the example shows one job reaching itself, not 'a change to one job can reach the others' (summary 2). The diagram adds to this: F looks like a fifth box hanging off totalVnd, outside the four jobs.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after the four-jobs sentence saying where the shipping fee belongs (e.g. 'the fee is its own pricing rule, next to the discount') and that discount and fee are two rules that can change separately; name that node in the diagram accordingly.

issues.quote: Where each piece of work lives is a large part of that cost for the changes that come later.
issues.text: Nothing before this sentence shows a different placement. I cannot reconstruct why moving the fee somewhere else would have made the discount edit cheaper or less surprising — the fee would still need a total. The conclusion (also summary line 5) is asserted, not shown.
issues.fix: Add one sentence before it saying concretely what a different placement would change, e.g. if the fee rule sat in its own named function that received the total, the caller would have to choose which total to pass, so the dependency would be visible instead of hidden in line order.

issues.quote: A week later, a loyal customer who ordered two items at 1,100,000 VND each asks why their shipping fee disappeared.
issues.text: The lesson never says whether the vanished fee is what the shop wanted. If not, the edit introduced a bug — but section 6 and q2 (option d explanation: 'The lesson's point is not hidden bugs') say the code behaved as written and the issue is not bugs. I am stuck on: was this a bug, or just a surprise?
issues.fix: Add one sentence at the end of section 2 or in section 4 saying whether the shop meant the fee to follow the discounted total, and that the point is nobody could tell from the code before editing.

issues.quote: The code ran exactly as written before the edit and after it; what changed is how much you had to know to edit it safely.
issues.text: 'What changed' confused me: how much you had to know did not change with the edit — it was always the same; the edit only revealed it. Also 'ran exactly as written' is true of all code, so it did not tell me anything.
issues.fix: Replace the second half with 'what the edit revealed is how much you had to know to change it safely'.

issues.quote: The price calculation builds up `totalVnd` in several steps, and the lines after the discount that read `totalVnd` see the discounted value — the shipping fee, which is only added when the total is below 2,000,000 VND, and the saving line.
issues.text: I had to read this sentence twice: the dash list after 'discounted value' carries a nested clause about the threshold, so I lost which lines are being listed.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: 'Every line after the discount that reads `totalVnd` sees the discounted value: the shipping fee and the saving line. The fee is only added when the total is below 2,000,000 VND.'

issues.quote: The file's own comment names the problem: "Four reasons to change one place, and no name for any of the four."
issues.text: Neither code block (lines 8-22, 24-34) contains this comment, so I looked for it and could not find it. The prose quotes it, so I am not stuck, only distracted.
issues.fix: Say where the comment is: 'The comment above the method names the problem: …'.

issues.quote: design — the choices about where each piece of work lives and what it can reach
issues.text: 'what it can reach' is vague in the definition; the lesson never comes back to 'what a piece of work can reach' (only to what a change can reach).
issues.fix: Replace 'what it can reach' with 'which variables and data it shares with other work', matching how section 4 uses it.

issues.quote: The fee is decided from `totalVnd` after the discount has already changed it, so a smaller discount can lift the total over the threshold
issues.text: Option a is about twice as long and much more specific than b, c, d; I could pick it by length alone. c ('recompiles', 'cached value') is obviously off-topic.
issues.fix: Shorten a (e.g. 'The fee line reads `totalVnd` after the discount has changed it') or make b/d equally specific.

issues.quote: False, because tests describe what the code does now, while design decides how costly the next change is.
issues.text: Near-verbatim of section 6 ('Tests check what the code does today; design decides how much you must understand to change it tomorrow') and summary line 4; answerable by matching words.
issues.fix: Reword c to apply the idea to Place, e.g. 'False: Place worked before and after the edit, yet the edit still changed the fee unexpectedly.'

issues.quote: The notification still sits in the same method as checking, pricing and saving, so adding SMS still means editing and re-checking all of it.
issues.text: Only a is plausible and it is the longest; b, c, d are easy to reject. Also 'editing … all of it' overstates: I would edit one line near the email line, and only re-read the rest.
issues.fix: Change to 'still means reading and re-checking all of it' and make one wrong option plausible (e.g. 'Renaming makes the email line easier to find, which is what the SMS change needs').

issues.quote: Renaming would matter when it changed behaviour, but a rename done consistently leaves results identical
issues.text: The 'would matter when … were' pattern in the b, c, d explanations reads oddly; I had to re-read each to get the point.
issues.fix: Use 'if': 'Renaming would matter if it changed behaviour, …'; same for c and d.
